title: If You Liked Squid Game, Watch These Next
intro: Squid Game worked on three frequencies simultaneously: survival spectacle, class-war allegory, and Korean character drama. Most shows that scratch one of those itches fail at the other two. This list maps to all three: pure survival tension, the kind of social critique that uses genre as a delivery mechanism, and Korean series that trade on the same emotional ambition.

picks.title: The Glory
picks.one_line: Class violence and long-game revenge from the same Netflix Korea pipeline - slower than Squid Game but just as merciless in what it says about who gets protected and who doesn't.

picks.title: Alice in Borderland
picks.one_line: A Japanese survival game series that preceded Squid Game's global wave - the games are more puzzle-driven, the emotional stakes are just as brutal.

picks.title: The Platform (El hoyo)
picks.one_line: A Spanish prison tower where food descends one floor at a time and those at the top eat everything - a visual allegory for economic hierarchy so blunt it feels like provocation.

picks.title: Hunger Games (Film Series)
picks.one_line: The template that Squid Game genre fans almost certainly already know - listed here because the Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes prequel (2023) is the best entry since the original.

picks.title: Moving
picks.one_line: A Korean superhero-espionage saga from the writer of The Bourne Identity - massive scale, generational trauma, and action sequences that embarrass most theatrical releases.

picks.title: All of Us Are Dead
picks.one_line: High school zombie outbreak - less social allegory than Squid Game, more visceral horror, and it earns its 12-episode length with genuine character investment.

picks.title: Parasite
picks.one_line: Bong Joon-ho's Palme d'Or film is the feature-length version of Squid Game's class argument - a single family's infiltration of another turns into something irreversible.

picks.title: Mask Girl
picks.one_line: A Korean mini about an office worker who live-streams anonymously - the obsession with beauty and visibility that runs under Squid Game's surface is the explicit subject here.

faq.q: Is Alice in Borderland basically the same show as Squid Game?
faq.a: Same genre chassis, different engine. Squid Game is about class violence and collective complicity; Alice in Borderland is more interested in individual psychology and puzzle mechanics. The tone is colder, the characters are harder to love, and the game logic is more elaborate. Worth watching, and genuinely different enough to run back-to-back.

faq.q: Should I watch Parasite before or after Squid Game?
faq.a: Order doesn't matter - they're in conversation thematically but completely standalone. If you haven't seen Parasite, it's the higher-craft experience and a natural next step after Squid Game. Bong Joon-ho on economic violence is the same argument Hwang Dong-hyuk is making, compressed into two hours and elevated by twenty years of filmmaking experience.
